html:
SMTO-POL-0033 — This task would use more than 16 computers

GUID: 22ffd6f3-d20d-5889-87dc-56454cecb51b
Slug: gateway-selection-limit
Domain: POL · Subsystem: resource-access

What happened

  • The computers already chosen for this task plus the new ones SMTO wants would add up to more than 16. No computers were added and no access was given.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to do the work on fewer computers at a time, for example in groups of up to 16. The limit counts different computers in one task, not how many steps SMTO runs.
  2. For a new request, open the target menu (headed Execution target) and unselect any Gateways the work doesn't need before you send it. Every selected Gateway counts toward the 16, even if this request doesn't use it.
  3. Before you approve anything, read SMTO's reply to confirm which computers it will work on. This rejection didn't change the task's computers, and you shouldn't lose one the work actually needs.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows a permission card naming 16 or fewer computers, or continues with the ones already selected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't remove a computer the work really needs just to get under the limit; ask SMTO to split the work instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • request_resource_access was rejected because the task's selected Gateways plus the newly requested Gateway resources exceed sixteen distinct Gateways.

What this means

  • After removing already active resource grants, the controller compares the selected Gateway set with Gateway resources remaining in the request. A union larger than sixteen is rejected before consent publication. The limit concerns distinct Gateways, not the number of tools or operations.

Why this can happen

  • After removing already active resource grants, the controller compares the selected Gateway set with Gateway resources remaining in the request. A union larger than sixteen is rejected before consent publication. The limit concerns distinct Gateways, not the number of tools or operations.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the current Gateway selection and distinct Gateway IDs introduced by this resource request.

How to fix it

  • Reduce the union of the task's gateway_selection and the Gateway resources remaining in the request (after removing already active grants) to sixteen or fewer distinct Gateways. The limit counts Gateways, not tools or operations.
  • Reduce the task's selected Gateways or request fewer additional Gateways, then review the resulting scope.

Retry and execution caution

  • Retry the permission request after reducing its combined Gateway scope.

How to verify the fix

  • The combined selection contains at most sixteen Gateways before the permission question is opened.

What not to do

  • Do not silently drop a required Gateway or assume a rejected request changed the task selection.

Technical notes

  • The rejected request does not add Gateways or grant their authority.
  • No connection-health or execution outcome is established by this scope limit.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
